title: Processing ICES DATRAS Data for FishGlob
text: FishGlob database global compilation standardized scientific trawl survey data used study large-scale patterns marine fish biodiversity community structure. FishGlob harmonizes data multiple regional monitoring programs standardizing: taxonomic information sampling effort catch metrics (abundance biomass per unit area) dataset integrates numerous long-term fisheries-independent surveys, including several surveys available ICES DATRAS database. ICES DATRAS (Database Trawl Surveys) provides access standardized survey data collected European seas, including haul-level sampling information (HH), length distributions (HL), individual data (CA). DATRASextra package provides tools process raw DATRAS survey data generate outputs compatible FishGlob data structure. vignette demonstrates workflow : download DATRAS survey data harmonize clean_datras raw survey tables standardize species taxonomy estimate swept area biomass generate FishGlob-compatible datasets workflow can applied single species multiple species. illustration, vignette uses mini. example dataset containing 5 species across 4 surveys (BITS, BTS, EVHOE, NS-IBTS): Amblyraja radiata, Hippoglossoides platessoides, Lophius piscatorius, Trisopterus esmarkii, Lepidorhombus whiffiagonis
code: data("mini", package = "DATRASextra")

title: Constructing a prediction grid within a survey domain
text: Next, create boundary polygon covers survey area sea building concave hull around trawl points, buffering 10 km, removing land areas using coastline data Natural Earth.  create regular grid square polygons (0.1° x 0.1°) covers sea area defined . ensure predictions focus near actual trawl observations, filter grid cells whose centroids farther 20 km trawl observation. Finally, extract longitude latitude coordinates filtered grid create data frame ready spatial prediction.
code: ## Enable spherical geometry for accurate distance calculations sf_use_s2(TRUE)  ## Concave hull + 10 km buffer boundary <- st_buffer(   st_concave_hull(st_union(sf_points), ratio = 0.05),   dist = 10000  # buffer in meters )  ## Get coastline data and prepare land polygon coastline <- ne_countries(scale = 10, returnclass = "sf") coastline <- st_transform(coastline, crs = 4326) coastline <- st_make_valid(coastline) land <- st_union(coastline)  ## Subtract land from boundary to get sea-only polygon survey_at_sea <- st_difference(boundary, land)  ## Plot it plot(survey_at_sea) grid_resolution <- 0.1  ## Create a regular grid of points (not polygons) covering bounding box of survey_at_sea bbox <- st_bbox(survey_at_sea)  ## Create sequences of lon and lat (x and y) at regular intervals x_seq <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], by = grid_resolution) y_seq <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], by = grid_resolution)  ## Create all combinations (full rectangular grid) grid_points <- expand.grid(lon = x_seq, lat = y_seq)  ## Convert regular grid of points to sf object grid_sf <- st_as_sf(grid_points, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)  ## Filter: keep only points inside the sea polygon grid_sf <- grid_sf[st_within(grid_sf, survey_at_sea, sparse = FALSE)[,1], ]  ## Filter: keep only points within max_distance of any trawl point max_distance <- 20000  ## 20 km close_to_trawl <- st_is_within_distance(grid_sf, sf_points, dist = max_distance) grid_sf <- grid_sf[lengths(close_to_trawl) > 0, ]  ## Final prediction grid: dataframe with lon and lat coords <- st_coordinates(grid_sf) prediction_grid <- data.frame(   lon = coords[, "X"],   lat = coords[, "Y"] )  ## Check dataframe head(prediction_grid) #>           lon      lat #> 1 -0.06077592 49.54647 #> 2  0.03922408 49.54647 #> 3 -0.06077592 49.64647 #> 4  0.03922408 49.64647 #> 5  0.13922408 49.64647 #> 6 -0.06077592 49.74647  ## Plot grid plot(prediction_grid$lon, prediction_grid$lat,      pch = 16, col = "lightblue", cex = 0.6,      xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude") plot(st_geometry(sf_points), add = TRUE, col = "red", pch = 20) plot(land, add = TRUE, col = "grey80", border = NA) legend("topright",        legend = c("Prediction grid", "Trawl observations"),        col = c("lightblue", "red"),        bg = "white",        pch = 20,        pt.cex = 1) box(lwd = 1.5)
